The sum can be written as  

\[
S=\sum_{k=1}^{10}\sin\!\left(\frac{(2k-1)\pi}{24}\right)\sin\!\left(\frac{(2k+3)\pi}{24}\right)
   =\sum_{k=1}^{10}\frac12\Bigl[\cos\Bigl(\frac{-4\pi}{24}\Bigr)-\cos\Bigl(\frac{(4k+2)\pi}{24}\Bigr)\Bigr].
\]

Since \(\cos(-\pi/6)=\cos(\pi/6)=\sqrt3/2\), each term contributes  

\[
\frac{\sqrt3}{4}-\frac12\cos\!\Bigl(\frac{(4k+2)\pi}{24}\Bigr)
   =\frac{\sqrt3}{4}-\frac12\cos\!\Bigl(\frac{(2k+1)\pi}{12}\Bigr).
\]

Hence  

\[
S=10\cdot\frac{\sqrt3}{4}-\frac12\sum_{k=1}^{10}\cos\!\Bigl(\frac{(2k+1)\pi}{12}\Bigr)
   =\frac{5\sqrt3}{2}-\frac12\,C,
\]

where  

\[
C=\sum_{k=1}^{10}\cos\!\Bigl(\frac{(2k+1)\pi}{12}\Bigr)
  =\cos\frac{3\pi}{12}+\cos\frac{5\pi}{12}+\dots+\cos\frac{21\pi}{12}.
\]

Evaluating the ten cosine values (using the exact forms for multiples of \(15^\circ\) and \(45^\circ\)) gives  

\[
C= -\frac{\sqrt6+\sqrt2}{2}.
\]

Therefore  

\[
S=\frac{5\sqrt3}{2}-\frac12\Bigl(-\frac{\sqrt6+\sqrt2}{2}\Bigr)
  =\frac{5\sqrt3}{2}+\frac{\sqrt6+\sqrt2}{4}
  =\frac{10\sqrt3+\sqrt6+\sqrt2}{4}.
\]

The proposed solution omitted the extra term \(\frac{\sqrt6+\sqrt2}{4}\), so the final answer \(\frac{5\sqrt3}{2}\) is incomplete.
